teaser.text: American International Group, or AIG, sells protection against financial risks that businesses and people cannot comfortably carry alone. Its business is a promise: if a covered event causes a covered loss, AIG will pay according to the policy.

paragraphs.text: The weighted price is $72.49 in October 2027, an 8% loss including dividends. It is $104.04 in October 2029, a 36% gain including dividends. Bear, base, and bull probabilities are 25%, 55%, and 20%.

blocks.heading: What has to go right for AIG, and what could go wrong?

paragraphs.text: The bear case assumes weaker property pricing, casualty reserve strengthening and higher catastrophe losses. The bull case requires profitable renewals, Convex participation, expense progress and no material adverse claims development. AIG’s below-30% expense-ratio objective supports the bull case, but it remains an operating target rather than GAAP earnings guidance.

blocks.heading: How much cash does AIG really make?

paragraphs.text: AIG’s investment income was $4,215 million in 2025. Net income was $3,096 million, while core earnings, AIG’s own measure, were $4,044 million. The gap matters because bond income, private-market valuations, taxes, corporate costs and transactions do not have the same repeatability.

Continuing operations generated $3,314 million of operating cash in 2025, close to net income of $3,096 million. But premiums arrive before many claims, so current cash can precede a reserve shortfall. The next test is how assets and debt support those obligations.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for AIG today?

paragraphs.text: The price-to-earnings ratio, or P/E, compares the share price with earnings per share. Reported earnings include every accounting gain and loss recorded during the period; core earnings remove items management considers unusual or unrelated to the continuing insurance operation. In second-quarter 2026, diluted earnings were $1.78 per share and adjusted earnings were $2.00. AIG’s lower core multiple is useful only if the excluded investment movements are temporary and the earnings left behind continue after the Corebridge sale.

dividend.closing: The full memo also explains AIG’s business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: How much does AIG pay in dividends?

paragraphs.text: Dividends remain stable in the bear case, grow moderately in the base case and sustain management’s near-term growth objective in the bull case. Base dividends rise from $1.93 per share in 2027 to $2.13 in 2029. The bear case holds at $1.75, while the bull case reaches $2.56.

The latest completed-year dividend was $1.75, and the stated target is at least 10% growth through 2026. A 2025 payout of $976 million against $3,096 million of net income leaves room for increases, but claims volatility argues for slower growth after 2026.

blocks.heading: What is AIG’s dividend yield at today’s price?

paragraphs.text: American International Group (AIG) is an insurer, so its stock price rests on promises that may not be settled for years. At $80.74 on October 19, 2026, the shares look cheap on some measures, but the central question is what kind of earnings and capital that price assumes.

earnings.opening: AIG’s next results are expected on November 3, 2026. The key thing to watch is whether AIG can turn premium growth into profitable underwriting while keeping reserve surprises contained.
earnings.closing: The full memo also explains AIG’s business, its rivals, its management and its risks.

blocks.heading: What has AIG guided for the year?

paragraphs.text: AIG’s weighted path is an 8% loss by October 2027 or a 36% gain by October 2029, hinging on repeatable underwriting and expense progress. Management targets at least 20.0% annual operating EPS growth compounded over 2025–2027 and Core Operating ROE of 10.0%–13.0% over that period. It also aims for a General Insurance expense ratio below 30.0% during 2025–2027 and dividend per share growth over 2025–2026.

blocks.heading: Did AIG keep its past promises?

paragraphs.text: AIG promised core operating return on equity of 10%–13% during 2025–2027 and an expense ratio below 30% by the end of that period. It delivered 11.1% Core Operating ROE in 2025, while its expense ratio was 31.1%. Andersen reaffirmed those commitments in August 2026, so they are obligations he inherits rather than achievements he can already claim.

blocks.heading: How have AIG’s revenue and profit trended?

paragraphs.text: The combined ratio improved to 89.0% from 89.3%, and core earnings rose to $1,069 million. Net income fell to $948 million, while diluted EPS fell to $1.78. The main weakness was investment-related, not an underwriting collapse.

blocks.heading: What should I watch in AIG’s next results?

paragraphs.text: The nearest checkpoint is AIG’s November 3, 2026 results and November 4 call. Investors should compare premium growth, expenses and the accident-year underwriting result.

Year-end 2026 should reveal more about Everest renewals and expenses. Convex participation then rises in 2027 and again in 2028. The key is to keep current underwriting, old-claim revisions and accounting recognition separate. That discipline leads to AIG’s operational bet on artificial intelligence.
